History and Physical (Detailed)

Consult Summary:
Adult female with no significant past medical history presents with a 3-day history of persistent, severe, right-predominant headache with photophobia and transient visual “shooting lights,” partially relieved by ibuprofen; clinical impression is likely migraine, and she is advised an urgent in-person neurological examination, trial of stronger NSAID + paracetamol, and red-flag safety-netting.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Blinding” headache for 3 days.  
• Onset/progression: Sudden onset on waking 3 days ago; constant since.  
• Location/quality: Generalized but maximal over right eye; described as stabbing/pressure; pain 8/10, improves to ~5/10 with ibuprofen.  
• Aggravating factors: Bright light; sudden standing; rapid head movement.  
• Relieving factors: Partial, temporary relief with ibuprofen; able to sleep through night.  
• Associated Sx: Photophobia; intermittent “shooting light” visual phenomenon; mild nausea (no vomiting).  
• Pertinent negatives: No focal weakness, numbness, speech difficulty, smell/taste change, fever, sinus/URTI symptoms, cough, weight change, nocturnal awakening, aura in past headaches.  
• Impact: Unable to focus on work from home; missed 1.5 workdays.

Past Medical History:
• Childhood abdominal pain—self-resolved, no diagnosis.  
• No chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
• Combined oral contraceptive pill – specific brand/dose/route/frequency not documented (started 1 yr ago).  
• Ibuprofen PRN for headache – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• No other regular or PRN medications.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives alone.  
• Occupation: Works from home.  
• Smoking: Never smoker.  
• Alcohol: Drinks ≈3 drinks once per week.  
• Recreational drugs: Denies.  
• Recent travel: None.

Family History:
• Mother: Migraine with vomiting.  
• No other significant family history reported.

Physical Examination:
(Not performed during virtual consult.)

Investigations:
None to date.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Persistent severe headache, likely migraine vs other secondary cause.  
  • Arrange urgent in-person appointment for full neurological exam, fundoscopy, and blood pressure check.  
  • Prescribe a stronger NSAID (agent not specified) to be taken with food; advise concurrent paracetamol.  
  • Educate on red-flag symptoms—worsening pain, change in character, neurological deficits, inability to tolerate oral intake, or new visual changes—seek A&E if occur.  
  • Continue current COC pill for now; discuss potential change if migraines with visual aura confirmed.  
  • Reassess after examination; consider further investigations (e.g., imaging) or specialist referral if indicated.

General Plan items:
• Safety-netting provided; patient to call clinic or emergency services as needed.  
• Follow-up: Booked via support team; appointment to be cancelled if symptoms fully resolve beforehand.

Quality checks:
• Missing but expected: Vitals, physical examination findings, medication reconciliation with doses, detailed headache diary.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Occasional inaudible segments/redactions; key clinical information largely intact.
